newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean court sentences five more students.
newsitem.headline: South Korean court sentences five more students.

text.p: A Seoul court on Tuesday jailed four students and handed a suspended prison term to another for taking part in violent pro-North Korean campus protests in August, a court official said.

This brings to 225 the number of students sentenced in connection with the demonstrations at Seoul's Yonsei University, in which one riot policeman was killed and hundreds of other officers and students injured.
The four students were jailed for between 1-1/2 and two years for taking part in an illegal protest, engaging in acts of violence and obstructing police in their duty, the official said.
The suspended jail term was for two years.
A total of 444 students were sent to trial at different courthouses.

Riot police stormed Yonsei to end a seven-day occupation of two teaching blocks by militant students taking part in an annual pro-Korean unification rally and demanding the withdrawal of 37,000 U.S. troops stationed in South Korea.
